claims.text: For graduate researchers and research theses, digital assistance and GenAI use is strictly limited to minor editorial support (language, clarity, spelling, grammar) under the Australian Standards for Editing Practice; substantial redrafting is prohibited and supervisor AI review requires explicit written permission.

Substantial redrafting of whole paragraphs or larger sections, or translating a substantial body of text into English, falls outside those limits.

coursework.en: At the University of Melbourne, each Subject Coordinator sets the boundaries of appropriate GenAI use in their subject; students must check before using AI for assessment-related work and produce the submitted work themselves unless explicitly authorized.
coursework.zh: 在墨尔本大学，由各课程主管教师确定本课程及考核作业中生成式 AI 的使用边界；学生在将 AI 用于考核作业前须查验明确许可，且除获准情形外须独立完成提交作品。

exams.en: In University of Melbourne examinations, students must verify whether GenAI is authorised by the Subject Coordinator or exam instructions, and if permitted, use only approved tools and specified permitted uses. Tool access conveys no exam authorization, and unauthorised or undisclosed AI use in exams constitutes academic misconduct under MPF1310.
exams.zh: 在墨尔本大学的考试中，学生必须查验本场考试是否经课程主管教师或考试大纲明确授权使用 GenAI；如获许可，仅能使用核准工具及限定用途。拥有校内工具权限不代表获准在考试中使用，未经授权或未披露在考试中使用 AI 构成 MPF1310 学术不端。

disclosure.en: University of Melbourne guidance mandates a dual disclosure framework: citing AI outputs in the reference list when quoting or paraphrasing does not replace an acknowledgement declaration; students must provide both a citation and a process declaration describing how tools were used, with unauthorised or undisclosed use constituting misconduct under MPF1310.
disclosure.zh: 墨尔本大学实行双重披露机制：在参考文献中引用或转述 AI 输出不能替代使用声明；学生既须规范引用，又须附具过程性声明详细说明工具使用环节。未经授权或未加披露使用 AI 构成 MPF1310 学术不端。

privacy_data.en: Students and researchers must not upload personal data, private information, third-party copyright, or patentable IP to external AI platforms. University teaching and assessment IP must remain within SparkAI or sanctioned environments; student LMS interactions and AILA session metadata are retained and reviewable by authorized decision-makers under the LMS privacy collection notice.
privacy_data.zh: 学生与研究人员严禁向外部 AI 平台上传个人隐私、第三方版权或可申请专利的成果。课程考核与教学材料仅能在 SparkAI 或校内核准平台处理；学生在 LMS 内的交互记录及 AILA 会话元数据依法保留，授权决策人员可在调查时进行核查。

approved_tools.en: The University of Melbourne provides AILA within Canvas LMS where enabled by coordinators, SparkAI as a secure internal platform for staff (student access prohibited), Turnitin AI writing detection as an investigative diagnostic in similarity reports, and M365 Copilot Chat for student study support. Institutional access conveys neither coursework nor examination permission.
approved_tools.zh: 墨尔本大学在教师启用的 Canvas 课程中提供 AILA 学习助手，为教职员工提供安全的 SparkAI 内部平台（禁止学生访问），在查重报告中提供 Turnitin AI 检测作为核查线索，并为学生提供 M365 Copilot Chat。校方提供工具不代表获得作业或考试使用许可。

research_publication.en: Under section 5.11 of the Responsible Conduct of Research Policy (MPF1318) and active University guidance, researchers must document DAT use, disclose tools in outputs, and obtain privacy/security/ethics approvals. For graduate research theses, AI editing is strictly restricted to minor language and clarity support under Australian Standards for Editing Practice, with supervisor AI review requiring explicit written candidate consent.
research_publication.zh: 依据现行《负责任科研行为准则》（MPF1318）第 5.11 条及校方指导，科研人员必须如实记录数字辅助工具使用、在科研成果中披露并取得隐私、安全与伦理审批。针对研究生毕业论文，AI 编辑严格限定为符合澳大利亚编辑标准的微调语言与润色，严禁实质性代写重写，导师使用 AI 审阅论文必须取得学生明确书面许可。

academic_integrity.en: Under MPF1310, unauthorised or undisclosed technology use in assessable work constitutes academic misconduct. Poor Academic Practice is managed educatively by Subject Coordinators, distinct from formal Faculty Level 1 and Serious Level 2 misconduct. Turnitin AI detection reports serve as an investigative prompt rather than proof, students have the right to provide drafts and explanations in exploratory discussions, and MPF1323 establishes a 20-university-business-day appeal window.
academic_integrity.zh: 依据 MPF1310，在考核作业中未经许可或未加披露使用技术构成学术不端。良好学术素养欠缺（Poor Academic Practice）由教师开展教育性纠正，与正式的一级及二级学术不端严格区分。Turnitin AI 检测报告仅作为调查线索而非违纪证据，学生有权在探索性讨论中解释成果并提交草稿，MPF1323 设立 20 个大学工作日的申诉窗口。

teaching_guidance.en: Melbourne teaching guidance advises Subject Coordinators to establish clear subject AI boundaries, model transparency, and provide guidance on translation and editing tool limits. GenAI tools must never substitute for staff evaluative judgement in marking or grading. Subjects are designed with at least 50% secure assessments to assure learning, supported by CSHE pedagogical assessment enhancement strategies.
teaching_guidance.zh: 墨尔本大学教学指引建议课程主管教师明确课程 AI 边界、以身作则披露使用，并就翻译与编辑工具的使用限度提供指导。生成式 AI 绝不能替代教师在评分考核中的学术评价判断。课程设计原则上要求至少 50% 安全考核以保障学习成效，并由 CSHE 提供考核优化教学策略。

security_procurement.en: The University of Melbourne AI Principles establish an overarching governance framework emphasizing fairness, literacy, privacy, and security; staff testing of assessment materials must remain within SparkAI or sanctioned environments rather than public third-party services.
security_procurement.zh: 墨尔本大学 AI 原则在素养、公平、隐私与安全等维度建立顶层治理框架；教职员工审阅教学考核材料必须在 SparkAI 或校方核准平台进行，严禁使用公开消费级第三方服务。

privacy_data.zh: 学生与研究人员严禁向外部 AI 平台上传个人隐私、第三方版权或可申请专利的成果。课程考核与教学材料仅能在 SparkAI 或校内核准平台处理；学生在 LMS 内的交互记录及 AILA 会话元数据依法保留，授权决策人员可在调查时进行核查。
privacy_data.meaningEn: Subject-level assessment guidelines; Student Academic Integrity Policy (MPF1310); Student Appeals Policy (MPF1323); Responsible Conduct of Research Policy (MPF1318 cl 5.11); Open-book exams advice; Canvas LMS privacy notice.
privacy_data.meaningZh: 区分课程大纲具体规定、学生学术诚信制度（MPF1310）、学生申诉规定（MPF1323）、负责任科研行为准则（MPF1318 第 5.11 条）、开卷考试指南及 Canvas LMS 隐私通告。

approved_tools.en: The University of Melbourne provides AILA within Canvas LMS where enabled by coordinators, SparkAI as a secure internal platform for staff (student access prohibited), Turnitin AI writing detection as an investigative diagnostic in similarity reports, and M365 Copilot Chat for student study support. Institutional access conveys neither coursework nor examination permission.
approved_tools.zh: 墨尔本大学在教师启用的 Canvas 课程中提供 AILA 学习助手，为教职员工提供安全的 SparkAI 内部平台（禁止学生访问），在查重报告中提供 Turnitin AI 检测作为核查线索，并为学生提供 M365 Copilot Chat。校方提供工具不代表获得作业或考试使用许可。
approved_tools.meaningEn: Subject-level assessment guidelines; Student Academic Integrity Policy (MPF1310); Student Appeals Policy (MPF1323); Responsible Conduct of Research Policy (MPF1318 cl 5.11); Open-book exams advice; Canvas LMS privacy notice.
approved_tools.meaningZh: 区分课程大纲具体规定、学生学术诚信制度（MPF1310）、学生申诉规定（MPF1323）、负责任科研行为准则（MPF1318 第 5.11 条）、开卷考试指南及 Canvas LMS 隐私通告。

research_publication.en: Under section 5.11 of the Responsible Conduct of Research Policy (MPF1318) and active University guidance, researchers must document DAT use, disclose tools in outputs, and obtain privacy/security/ethics approvals. For graduate research theses, AI editing is strictly restricted to minor language and clarity support under Australian Standards for Editing Practice, with supervisor AI review requiring explicit written candidate consent.
research_publication.zh: 依据现行《负责任科研行为准则》（MPF1318）第 5.11 条及校方指导，科研人员必须如实记录数字辅助工具使用、在科研成果中披露并取得隐私、安全与伦理审批。针对研究生毕业论文，AI 编辑严格限定为符合澳大利亚编辑标准的微调语言与润色，严禁实质性代写重写，导师使用 AI 审阅论文必须取得学生明确书面许可。
research_publication.meaningEn: Subject-level assessment guidelines; Student Academic Integrity Policy (MPF1310); Student Appeals Policy (MPF1323); Responsible Conduct of Research Policy (MPF1318 cl 5.11); Open-book exams advice; Canvas LMS privacy notice.
research_publication.meaningZh: 区分课程大纲具体规定、学生学术诚信制度（MPF1310）、学生申诉规定（MPF1323）、负责任科研行为准则（MPF1318 第 5.11 条）、开卷考试指南及 Canvas LMS 隐私通告。

academic_integrity.en: Under MPF1310, unauthorised or undisclosed technology use in assessable work constitutes academic misconduct. Poor Academic Practice is managed educatively by Subject Coordinators, distinct from formal Faculty Level 1 and Serious Level 2 misconduct. Turnitin AI detection reports serve as an investigative prompt rather than proof, students have the right to provide drafts and explanations in exploratory discussions, and MPF1323 establishes a 20-university-business-day appeal window.
academic_integrity.zh: 依据 MPF1310，在考核作业中未经许可或未加披露使用技术构成学术不端。良好学术素养欠缺（Poor Academic Practice）由教师开展教育性纠正，与正式的一级及二级学术不端严格区分。Turnitin AI 检测报告仅作为调查线索而非违纪证据，学生有权在探索性讨论中解释成果并提交草稿，MPF1323 设立 20 个大学工作日的申诉窗口。
academic_integrity.meaningEn: Subject-level assessment guidelines; Student Academic Integrity Policy (MPF1310); Student Appeals Policy (MPF1323); Responsible Conduct of Research Policy (MPF1318 cl 5.11); Open-book exams advice; Canvas LMS privacy notice.
academic_integrity.meaningZh: 区分课程大纲具体规定、学生学术诚信制度（MPF1310）、学生申诉规定（MPF1323）、负责任科研行为准则（MPF1318 第 5.11 条）、开卷考试指南及 Canvas LMS 隐私通告。

teaching_guidance.en: Melbourne teaching guidance advises Subject Coordinators to establish clear subject AI boundaries, model transparency, and provide guidance on translation and editing tool limits. GenAI tools must never substitute for staff evaluative judgement in marking or grading. Subjects are designed with at least 50% secure assessments to assure learning, supported by CSHE pedagogical assessment enhancement strategies.
teaching_guidance.zh: 墨尔本大学教学指引建议课程主管教师明确课程 AI 边界、以身作则披露使用，并就翻译与编辑工具的使用限度提供指导。生成式 AI 绝不能替代教师在评分考核中的学术评价判断。课程设计原则上要求至少 50% 安全考核以保障学习成效，并由 CSHE 提供考核优化教学策略。
teaching_guidance.meaningEn: Subject-level assessment guidelines; Student Academic Integrity Policy (MPF1310); Student Appeals Policy (MPF1323); Responsible Conduct of Research Policy (MPF1318 cl 5.11); Open-book exams advice; Canvas LMS privacy notice.
teaching_guidance.meaningZh: 区分课程大纲具体规定、学生学术诚信制度（MPF1310）、学生申诉规定（MPF1323）、负责任科研行为准则（MPF1318 第 5.11 条）、开卷考试指南及 Canvas LMS 隐私通告。

security_procurement.en: The University of Melbourne AI Principles establish an overarching governance framework emphasizing fairness, literacy, privacy, and security; staff testing of assessment materials must remain within SparkAI or sanctioned environments rather than public third-party services.
security_procurement.zh: 墨尔本大学 AI 原则在素养、公平、隐私与安全等维度建立顶层治理框架；教职员工审阅教学考核材料必须在 SparkAI 或校方核准平台进行，严禁使用公开消费级第三方服务。
security_procurement.meaningEn: Subject-level assessment guidelines; Student Academic Integrity Policy (MPF1310); Student Appeals Policy (MPF1323); Responsible Conduct of Research Policy (MPF1318 cl 5.11); Open-book exams advice; Canvas LMS privacy notice.

do.en: Check your Subject Coordinator syllabus and specific examination instructions before using generative AI in exams or coursework.
do.zh: 在考试或学业成果中使用生成式 AI 前，仔细查验任课教师的大纲与具体考核要求。

do.en: Provide both a reference list citation when quoting/paraphrasing AI outputs and an acknowledgement declaration describing process assistance.
do.zh: 直接引用或转述 AI 输出时在参考文献中注明出处，并同时附具过程性使用声明说明工具使用环节。

do.en: Document digital assistance tool (DAT) research use, disclose DAT use to partners, collaborators, and in publications/theses, and obtain all necessary approvals (including privacy, security, or ethics review where applicable) under MPF1318 cl 5.11.
do.zh: 依据 MPF1318 第 5.11 条，记录数字辅助工具（DAT）研究使用，向合作方及在出版物与论文等成果中披露，并在适用时取得所有必要审批（包括隐私、安全或伦理审查）。

dont.en: Do not upload personal information, student records, confidential research, or third-party copyright materials to unauthorized public AI tools.
dont.zh: 切勿向未经授权的公开 AI 工具输入个人信息、学生记录、保密科研数据或第三方版权教学材料。

dont.en: Do not assume institutional tool access (AILA, SparkAI, M365 Copilot Chat) conveys permission for course assignments or examinations.
dont.zh: 切勿将学校开通某款 AI 工具（如 AILA、SparkAI、Copilot Chat）等同于获准将其用于课程作业或考试。

dont.en: Do not use generative AI tools in examinations or assessable work without Subject Coordinator authorization or disclosure, which constitutes academic misconduct under MPF1310.
dont.zh: 切勿在未获任课教师明确许可或未加披露的情况下在考试或学业成果中使用生成式 AI 工具，否则构成 MPF1310 学术不端。

claim-university-of-melbourne-5.text: At the University of Melbourne, using GenAI tools on an assessment task that does not permit them, or using them in preparation without acknowledgement, constitutes academic misconduct under cl. 4.13 of the Student Academic Integrity Policy (MPF1310).
claim-university-of-melbourne-5.scope: Student academic integrity and disciplinary procedures

evidence.quote: It’s important your students realise that if an assessment task does not permit the use of such tools, or if they use such tools in the preparation of an assessment submission without acknowledgement, this constitutes academic misconduct under cl. 4.13 of the Student Academic Integrity Policy (MPF1310).
evidence.location: Section: University policies in relation to Generative AI; extracted text lines 57-57

claim-university-of-melbourne-10.text: A high AI score in Turnitin's writing detection report is not proof of misconduct and does not on its own constitute grounds for making an allegation of academic misconduct.
claim-university-of-melbourne-10.scope: Turnitin AI score interpretation and misconduct threshold

evidence.quote: A high AI score in Turnitin’s writing detection report is not proof that academic misconduct has taken place (any more than would be the case when using the more familiar similarity report tool to flag potential plagiarism).  It does not, on its own, constitute grounds for making an allegation of academic misconduct.
evidence.location: Section: Turnitin Writing Detection Guidance; extracted text lines 37-37

cl-the-university-of-melbourne-instituti.text: AILA is listed for The University of Melbourne in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: conditionally allowed. Derived endorsement type: self_hosted_system.
cl-the-university-of-melbourne-instituti.scope: Canvas LMS student chatbot developed by Product Innovation Team

evidence.quote: The University’s Product Innovation Team has developed the AI learning assistant (AILA): a chatbot embedded in the LMS and intended as a learning resource for students.
evidence.location: Section: AI Learning Assistant (AILA); extracted text lines 80-80

cl-the-university-of-melbourne-instituti.text: SparkAI is listed for The University of Melbourne in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: conditionally allowed. Derived endorsement type: self_hosted_system.
cl-the-university-of-melbourne-instituti.scope: Secure internal staff platform (spark.unimelb.edu.au); student access prohibited

evidence.quote: SparkAI is a secure platform internal to the University of Melbourne that can be accessed by staff (but not by students). It allows staff to explore Generative AI tools and capabilities using information that may be sensitive to the University, such as teaching/assignment materials, potentially copyrighted material, or other data that have Intellectual Property overlays.
evidence.location: Section: SparkAI Platform; extracted text lines 67-67

cl-the-university-of-melbourne-turnitin-.text: Turnitin AI writing detection is listed for The University of Melbourne in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: conditionally allowed. Derived endorsement type: institutionally_licensed_or_procured.
cl-the-university-of-melbourne-turnitin-.scope: Canvas similarity report staff diagnostic (not a student generative tool)

evidence.quote: Turnitin’s AI writing detection tool is currently accessible to staff within Canvas as part of its similarity report function, for work submitted in English.
evidence.location: Section: Turnitin AI Detection; extracted text lines 32-32

claim-university-of-melbourne-1.text: Before using GenAI for assessment-related work, University of Melbourne students must check that their Subject Coordinator has authorised its use.

evidence.quote: Before you use GenAI for assessment-related work you must check to ensure that your Subject Coordinator has authorised its use.
evidence.location: Section: Is it okay to use GenAI at Melbourne?; extracted text lines 6-6

claim-university-of-melbourne-11.text: Because third-party external platforms such as ChatGPT use prompts and inputs to further train their models, University of Melbourne staff must not enter assessments, teaching materials, or sensitive IP into third-party platforms, reserving such testing for SparkAI or sanctioned platforms.
claim-university-of-melbourne-11.scope: External platform data retention and teaching IP protection

evidence.quote: Since assessments and other teaching materials constitute University IP, they should never be tested on third-party external platforms such as ChatGPT, since these platforms use all prompts and inputs to further train their models.  Any such testing/auditing must be done only within the University’s secure GenAI platform (SparkAI) or other University of Melbourne-sanctioned platforms.
evidence.location: Section: Data Privacy and AI Training Risks; extracted text lines 41-41

claim-university-of-melbourne-12.text: If students use an AI tool such as ChatGPT to generate output that is paraphrased or directly quoted in assessable writing, it must be cited and referenced as a source in the reference list.
claim-university-of-melbourne-12.scope: Assessment citation and reference list formatting

evidence.quote: If you have used an AI tool or technology such as ChatGPT to generate an output which you either paraphrase or direct quote in your writing, you must cite and reference this output as a source in your reference list.
evidence.location: Section: Citing AI Output in Reference List; extracted text lines 15-15

claim-university-of-melbourne-15.text: Generative AI tools can only be used in research outputs if material generated or substantially altered is acknowledged according to University policy and the Australian Code for the Responsible Conduct of Research.
claim-university-of-melbourne-15.scope: Research publication and Code for Responsible Conduct

evidence.quote:
This clarifies
that generative AI tools can only be used if material that is generated or substantially altered by these tools is
acknowledged according to the University’s policy and the Australian Code for the Responsible Conduct of Research.
evidence.location: Section: Inquiry Submission - Research Conduct; extracted text lines 229-231

claim-university-of-melbourne-16.text: Researchers are advised not to share confidential information or innovation details in generative AI prompts, as that may cause IP to no longer be owned by the researcher or University.
claim-university-of-melbourne-16.scope: Research confidentiality, data, and patentable inventions

evidence.quote:
The University has advised researchers that they should
not share confidential information or information about an innovation  in a generative AI prompt, as that may mean
that the IP is no longer owned by the researcher or by the University.
evidence.location: Section: Inquiry Submission - Commercial IP and Confidentiality; extracted text lines 252-254

claim-university-of-melbourne-2.text: University of Melbourne students must protect personal information and not upload full names, dates of birth, addresses, or other confidential, sensitive or private information to GenAI tools.

evidence.quote: Protect your personal information and that of others. Do not upload your full name, date of birth, address or other confidential, sensitive or private information.
evidence.location: Section: Protecting Personal Information; extracted text lines 44-44

claim-university-of-melbourne-3.text: When uploading material to an AI tool, University of Melbourne students must ensure they do not violate creator copyright without permission.

evidence.quote: When you upload this material to an AI tool, you may be violating the copyright of creators who have not given permission to do this with their material.
evidence.location: Section: Respecting Copyright; extracted text lines 47-47

claim-university-of-melbourne-6.text: Each University of Melbourne subject coordinator is responsible for setting out the bounds of appropriate GenAI use within their subject and having conversations with students for clarity.

evidence.quote: It follows that it is the responsibility of each subject coordinator to set out the bounds of appropriate GenAI use within their subject. Coordinators are strongly encouraged to consider possible use case scenarios for their assessments, set clear boundaries, and have conversations with their students to enable clarity about what tools are appropriate and for what tasks.
evidence.location: Section: Setting Subject Boundaries; extracted text lines 58-58

claim-university-of-melbourne-7.text: Assessments and teaching materials constitute University IP and must never be tested on third-party external platforms like ChatGPT; testing or auditing must be done only within SparkAI or sanctioned platforms.
claim-university-of-melbourne-7.scope: Staff materials review and institutional IP

evidence.quote: Since assessments and other teaching materials constitute University IP, they should never be tested on third-party external platforms such as ChatGPT, since these platforms use all prompts and inputs to further train their models.  Any such testing/auditing must be done only within the University’s secure GenAI platform (SparkAI) or other University of Melbourne-sanctioned platforms.
evidence.location: Section: Protecting University Intellectual Property; extracted text lines 41-41

claim-university-of-melbourne-9.text: At the University of Melbourne, use of GenAI tools for marking or grading should never be a substitute for staff exercising their own evaluative judgement.
claim-university-of-melbourne-9.scope: Staff evaluative judgment and AI-assisted marking limits

evidence.quote: Use of GenAI tools should never be a substitute for staff exercising their own evaluative judgement.
evidence.location: Section: University policies in relation to Generative AI, subsection: Can staff use GenAI for marking/grading of student work?; extracted text lines 63-63

claim-university-of-melbourne-8.text: University of Melbourne staff may use GenAI tools to help prepare teaching materials provided care is exercised for proper use of University IP and ethical AI use.

evidence.quote: Staff can use GenAI tools to help in the preparation of teaching materials, however care must always be exercised to ensure proper use of university IP, and ethical use of GenAI.
evidence.location: Section: Staff Teaching Materials Preparation; extracted text lines 61-61

claim-university-of-melbourne-13.text: University of Melbourne staff should consider and provide advice on the limits of acceptable use of AI-powered translation and editing tools (e.g. Grammarly, Google Translate) in their subjects, as student use can extend to the point where students are no longer expressing their own ideas.
claim-university-of-melbourne-13.scope: Staff subject guidance on AI translation and editing boundaries

evidence.quote: Student use of these tools may pose risks to academic integrity, and staff should consider and provide advice on the limits of acceptable use in their subject. Use of these tools can easily extend to the point where students are no longer expressing their own ideas or understanding of the subject matter.
evidence.location: Section: AI and assessment, subsection: Is it okay if students use GenAI for language translation or editing their work?; extracted text lines 51-51

claim-university-of-melbourne-17.text: In its 2023 submission, the University encouraged optional government sector guidance and communities of practice to share best practice in GenAI education.
claim-university-of-melbourne-17.scope: Sector policy recommendations and communities of practice

evidence.quote:
Government may wish to develop optional guidance on the use of generative AI in the sector. The
Government could also establish communities of practice to share ideas , best practice and lessons learned in
generative AI in higher education.
evidence.location: Section: Inquiry Submission - Recommendations; extracted text lines 45-47

claim-university-of-melbourne-18.text: The Faculty of Architecture, Building and Planning (BEL+T) provides discipline-specific guidance offering educators key concepts and definitions for generative AI in built environments.
claim-university-of-melbourne-18.scope: Faculty disciplinary guidance in architecture and built environments

evidence.quote: This BEL+T Guidance on Generative AI (genAI) offers ABP subject coordinators, and other educators in built environments disciplines, some key concepts and definitions in this fast-developing space.
evidence.location: Section: BEL+T Guidance Scope; extracted text lines 4-4

claim-university-of-melbourne-4.text: At the University of Melbourne, students are expected to produce their own perspective, experience, and knowledge in assessable work rather than rely on AI output alone.

evidence.quote: While GenAI can produce seemingly valuable or original output, your own perspective, experience and knowledge is what the University and future employers expect. Therefore, knowing what value you add is crucial.
evidence.location: Section: Demonstrating Your Knowledge; extracted text lines 60-60

claim-university-of-melbourne-14.text: Specific guidance for University of Melbourne researchers regarding acknowledging digital assistance tools in research outputs is available via the Research Ethics and Integrity website.
claim-university-of-melbourne-14.scope: Research ethics and digital assistance tool guidance

evidence.quote: Researchers: Specific guidance for University of Melbourne researchers about how to acknowledge the use of digital assistance tools in research outputs is available at the Research ethics and integrity website.
evidence.location: Section: Guidance for Researchers; extracted text lines 8-8

claim-university-of-melbourne-citation-v.text: University of Melbourne guidance mandates that citing AI outputs in the reference list does not replace an acknowledgement declaration: students who cite or paraphrase AI outputs must still provide a declaration detailing how AI tools were used across the assessment process.
claim-university-of-melbourne-citation-v.scope: Dual requirement of citation and declaration for assessment submissions

evidence.quote:
I have cited and referenced outputs from an AI tool or technology in my assessment. Do I also need a declaration?
Yes. In addition to a citation or reference, a declaration provides you with an opportunity to describe how you have used an AI tool or technology to complete your assessment. This information assists your readers to understand how AI tools and technologies have been incorporated in your research, writing and learning processes.
evidence.location: Section: Acknowledging AI Tools (Declaration Requirement FAQ); extracted text lines 59-60

claim-university-of-melbourne-student-ex.text: In University of Melbourne examinations, students must verify whether GenAI use is authorised for the specific exam, and if permitted, ensure that only approved tools and specified uses are employed in alignment with University policy.
claim-university-of-melbourne-student-ex.scope: Student examination conduct and open-book exam rules

evidence.quote: Make sure you know whether the use of GenAI tools is authorised in the exam, and if so, which tools or specific uses are allowed
evidence.location: Section: Open-book exams advice - GenAI authorization check; extracted text lines 58-58

evidence.quote: If you use GenAI tools to assist in preparing or completing your exam, it is your responsibility to do so ethically, responsibly and in alignment with University of Melbourne policy.
evidence.location: Section: Open-book exams advice - Ethical responsibility; extracted text lines 60-60

claim-university-of-melbourne-exam-rules.text: Under University guidelines on assuring learning in the age of GenAI, in most cases subjects are designed so that secure assessment types account for at least 50% of total marks, with phased implementation (2026–2028) and programmatic exceptions.
claim-university-of-melbourne-exam-rules.scope: Assuring learning guidelines and secure assessment curriculum design

evidence.quote:
In most cases, this means designing subjects so that “secure” assessments, in which learning
is assured, account for at least 50% of a subject’s mark (Principle 1).
evidence.location: Section: Assuring Learning Guidelines Principle 1; extracted text lines 10-11

claim-university-of-melbourne-technology.text: The University of Melbourne academic misconduct framework explicitly categorizes unauthorized or undisclosed use of technology (including GenAI) as a breach type under academic integrity procedures.
claim-university-of-melbourne-technology.scope: Student Academic Integrity Policy breach categories

evidence.quote:
Breach types
Plagiarism
Unauthorised re-use of previous work (self plagiarism)
Breach of examination or assessment rules or directions
Falsification or misrepresentation of data
Unauthorised or undisclosed use of technology (incl. GenAI)
evidence.location: Section: Managing Suspected Academic Misconduct - Breach Types; extracted text lines 128-133

claim-university-of-melbourne-misconduct.text: Poor academic practice refers to minor and unintentional departures managed educatively by Subject Coordinators, and is explicitly distinct from academic misconduct.
claim-university-of-melbourne-misconduct.scope: Student Academic Integrity Policy procedural classifications

evidence.quote:
Poor academic practice refers to minor and unintentional departures from accepted scholarly conventions or failures to comply with assessment guidelines. Poor academic practice incidents are characterised by inexperience, lack of student knowledge, or poor academic skills, and does not compromise the purpose and/or integrity of the assessment.
Importantly, poor academic practice is not academic misconduct, may be treated as an assessment matter and managed within the marking and assessment guidelines set by the Board of Examiners for the subject.
evidence.location: Section: Poor Academic Practice Definition and Management; extracted text lines 66-67

claim-university-of-melbourne-turnitin-i.text: Turnitin AI detection results serve only as a prompt for further investigation; if suspected, students may be invited to explain their work and provide drafts or notes in an exploratory discussion.
claim-university-of-melbourne-turnitin-i.scope: Turnitin AI investigative procedures and student rights

evidence.quote:
As with the similarity report generated by Turnitin, the result of the AI writing detector tool is a prompt for further investigation.
